messages:
samira: Nightly eval failing badly on the long-context suite for the new quantized v2.3 candidate. Lots of cases where the instruction context gets dropped after ~8k tokens — outputs start answering as if the instruction was never there. Anyone else seeing KV-cache offset drift or truncation artifacts?

kai: Yup saw similar in local reproducer. Symptoms look like cache pointers getting shifted — generations include the last user turn but not the system instruction. :warning:

anya: Nightly logs have repeated warnings: `cache_index_mismatch` right before response generation for several prompts. Pasting snippet: 
```
[2026-06-10T03:12:45Z] WARN model_server: cache_index_mismatch: expected 12345 got 12288, seq_len=8192
[2026-06-10T03:12:45Z] DEBUG kvcache: dropping stale entries from 12288..12344
```

michael: Two quick possibilities: (1) tokenization change in tokenizer build used for quantization (off-by-one between encoding runs) (2) batching/concat code that computes KV offsets when resuming cache with streaming.

eval-bot: nightly-run v2.3-quantized-20260610: long-context-suite: 37 failing / 1200 tests (baseline v2.2: 3 failing). Top failure mode: "lost_system_instruction_after_8k". Related diffs: https://ci.internal/redwood/evals/20260610/longctx-diff

samira: Good catch on tokenizer mismatch. Kai — can you run the reproducer with tokenizer hash and dump token ids for the whole conversation? Use `--dump-tokens` and `--dump-kv` flags. Command: 
```
./repro_longctx.sh --model v2.3-quant --case id_482 --dump-tokens > /tmp/482.tokens
./repro_longctx.sh --model v2.3-quant --case id_482 --dump-kv > /tmp/482.kv
```

kai: Running now. Early glance: token counts line up but there is a block where `kv_index` jumps backward by 256. Sharing small excerpt: 
```
step 77: kv_index_start=12288 kv_index_end=20479
step 78: kv_index_start=12032 kv_index_end=20191  <-- back by 256
```

anya: That aligns with our autoscaler batching heuristic that pads to multiples of 256 for certain GPU kernels. If padding is applied after computing offsets, that would shift indices when merging cached blocks.

michael: Exactly — likely order is: compute offsets -> apply padding -> write KV, but consumers expect padding computed first. Need to inspect `runtime/batching/kv_merge.cpp` around offset math. I can take that.

ops: Heads up, canary rollout for v2.3 has been paused by CI because of the eval failures. Rolling back can be done if we confirm root cause quickly. :no_entry_sign:

samira: Priority: produce a small patch toggling padding-after-merge to padding-before-merge in the runtime and run the failing case. If tests pass, we can unpause canary and run extended nightly. Kai & Michael to pair. Any blockers?

kai: I can pair after lunch. I'll also diff tokenizer hashes between v2.2 and v2.3 to rule that out.

michael: Taking `runtime/batching` now. Found a suspicious function `apply_padding_to_kv()` called from `merge_kv_streams()` after `compute_offsets()`. I'll try swapping order and run unit tests.

eval-bot: quick-ci: runtime-batching-unit-tests: 312/315 passed locally for michael. Failing tests are related to expected buffer sizes.

anya: If those unit tests assume old behavior, we should update tests to reflect intended semantics and add new regression test for longctx cases. I'll add a nightly-only unit that simulates mixed padding and cached resumes.

samira: Thanks team. Plan: 1) Michael & Kai patch/test today, 2) Anya adds regression test, 3) If green, unpause canary and run a 6-hour smoke, 4) If smoke good, promote. Samira -> filing a ticket to track: INF-2981.

ops: Ticket INF-2981 created & linked to canary pipeline. I've also queued rollback playbook in case smoke fails.

michael: Patch up, tests updated. Local reproducer now returns instruction preserved for id_482. Pushing PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4321

kai: Tokenizer hashes match between v2.2 and v2.3 — good to rule that out.

samira: Awesome. Once CI runs the PR and nightly regression passes, we'll re-run full long-context suite. Thanks all. :tada:

eval-bot: PR check results: runtime/pull/4321: CI passed (unit + regressions), nightly-eval re-run scheduled.

last_update: samira: Nightly re-run shows failing count dropped to 4/1200, all are unrelated content-generation edgecases. Closing INF-2981 after patch merge and canary promote. :white_check_mark:
